teaser: The people I advise read through agents. Content needs a second package, a brief for their agent, and memory, so it reads what changed, not everything.
core_idea: Readers increasingly read through an agent. A founder gave an article on threat tiers to their agent, which saw the team defending against states while backups were undone and reset the target to T3. So content should travel by several routes: to the person, to their agent as a plain-text brief with the articles by number, reasons, graph slices and rules for critical reading, back from the agent to the person as a translation, and later agent to agent through an encrypted lane. Articles are compression we control, which keeps workflows affordable; an agent with an account and memory should read only the delta, which is what it would pay for. Packs must be written safely: data not instructions, nothing hidden, nothing that acts for us, disagreement invited.
